_comment: Written by dragon-dev-buddy:buddy-setup. Every skill in the pack reads this file.

project.name: buddy-mcp
project.what_it_is: A persistent coding companion for Claude Code served over MCP: hatches a buddy, grants XP as work is observed, and learns which of the user's skills fit which kind of task.
project.stack: TypeScript (ESM, NodeNext, strict + noUncheckedIndexedAccess) on Node >=24. @modelcontextprotocol/sdk over stdio transport, zod for tool-argument validation, node:sqlite for persistence. No framework, no HTTP server. Two runtime dependencies.
project.runtime: Node.js 24 and 26 (node:sqlite is unflagged from Node 24 onwards)
project.deploy_target: Local stdio subprocess launched by an MCP client. Packaged for npm (bin: buddy-mcp, buddy-import; files: dist) but not yet published.
project.data_store: SQLite at $BUDDY_HOME, defaulting to ~/.buddy-mcp. Deliberately not ~/.buddy, which belongs to @fiorastudio/buddy.

related_repos._comment: Repos this one is meaningfully entangled with. Declared, never inferred from disk adjacency -- ~/projects/DragonSecurity has 85 sibling directories and proximity means nothing. `path` is relative to this repo root and is the only field anything could ever resolve; its absence means the repo is not checked out on this machine. `url` is identity only, an opaque string (these remotes are scp-style and have no URL scheme). Read by the skills pack for context; the MCP server itself does not read this file.

repos.name: dragon-dev-buddy
repos.what: The skills pack and Claude Code plugin this server backs. Ships the MCP server config that spawns buddy-mcp, the skills that read this config.json, and the pre/post hooks that enforce the buddy_advise / buddy_observe calls. Go, plus skills/ and hooks/. A change to this server tool surface lands there, not here.

repos.name: fiorastudio/buddy
repos.what: NOT upstream and NOT a fork parent -- buddy-mcp shares no code with it and was written from scratch. Related only because the two collide in namespace: it owns ~/.buddy, which is why this server stores at ~/.buddy-mcp. PR #158 there is separate work of the author's. Easily conflated with this repo; treat any claim that buddy-mcp derives from it as wrong.

security._exposure_note: Public source repository, not yet published to npm. As of 2026-08-02 the process IS network-capable: `buddy-mcp serve` (src/serve.ts) binds node:http and exposes GET /status and /healthz. It defaults to 127.0.0.1 and must be given --host 0.0.0.0 to leave the machine; the endpoint is read-only, unauthenticated, and opens the SQLite database with readOnly:true. There is still no fetch, no outbound egress, no node:net client and no child_process in src/. Two things to revisit: (1) the moment a write route is added (a `pet` action is planned for a hardware display), unauthenticated LAN access stops being a presence leak and becomes a control surface, so it needs a shared secret compared with timingSafeEqual; (2) an npm release, at which point every installer runs this against their own transcripts.
security._data_sensitivity_note: The server reads ~/.claude/projects/**/*.jsonl (raw Claude Code transcripts), ~/.claude.json and ~/.buddy/buddy.db. Transcript content is arbitrary and may contain API keys, tokens or customer data pasted into a session. Derived text is persisted indefinitely to the SQLite DB. No egress is possible, which caps exploitability but not the class. Critically, this material never touches the git repository, so repository-level secret scanning is not a control that covers it.
security.auth_model: None. Runs as a stdio subprocess under the invoking user's identity and inherits their filesystem trust. Tool arguments are the only external input surface and are validated with zod.
trust_boundaries: MCP client -> server (stdio): tool arguments (summary, task, name, skills_used) are model-generated text crossing into the server. zod-validated with length and enum constraints.
~/.claude/projects/**/*.jsonl -> src/backfill.ts: untrusted, arbitrary-content transcript files parsed from disk and turned into persisted state.
~/.claude.json and ~/.buddy/buddy.db -> src/import.ts: third-party data (Anthropic's /buddy and @fiorastudio/buddy) read and imported into this server's own store.
Plugin, personal and project skill directories -> src/skills.ts: SKILL.md content authored by third parties, read from paths the server does not control.
npm registry -> installers: dormant until first publish, then the primary boundary. dist/ is the shipped artifact and is built by tsc in CI.
known_risk_areas: Transcript ingestion (src/backfill.ts): parses arbitrary JSONL from ~/.claude/projects and derives persisted text from it. Untrusted input, indefinite retention, and outside the boundary any repository secret scanner covers.

Skill discovery and path handling (src/skills.ts): reads SKILL.md from plugin, personal and project directories -- paths the server does not control, with third-party plugin content among them. Skills are keyed by (name, project_root), so path derivation is also a correctness boundary between repos.

engagement._comment: Empty by design: internal work on the author's own code, no offensive engagement. vuln-triage will not emit proof-of-concept exploit code and pentest-report will not produce a client deliverable while this block is empty.

practice._test_note: node --test test/*.test.js, running against dist/. npm run build must precede it.
practice._lint_note: No linter configured. tsc strict with noUncheckedIndexedAccess is the only static gate.
practice.ci: GitHub Actions (.github/workflows/ci.yml): build and test on Node 24 and 26, on pull_request and on push to main and renovate/**.
practice._tooling_note: No SAST and no secret scanner configured in this repo. The author's dragon-dev-buddy skills pack is the compensating control for keeping credentials out of git; note that it does not cover the ~/.buddy-mcp datastore.
